subject: Recap: Dedicated pool discovery - Tithonix Labs
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@tithonix.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Dedicated pool discovery - Tithonix Labs

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. I’ve left in-line asks where we need a confirmation from your side.

What we heard (pain points)
- Latency spikes in production during concurrent batch + online requests (current 99th ~750ms under peak load).
- Cost unpredictability with spot-backed instances today; finance wants a predictable monthly run-rate.
- Regulatory requirement: certain pipelines process PII and must remain isolated (VPC + customer-managed KMS, audit logs).

Current stack you described
- Triton + internal orchestrator on 4xA100s (on-prem colocation), inference endpoints behind Kong.
- S3 for model artifacts; custom tokenization service.
- Traffic: steady baseline with 3 sustained worker processes; occasional large bursts from batch jobs (approx 1-2 hrs, 2–3x baseline).

Success criteria for a Dedicated fit
- Baseline sustained throughput: ~800 requests/sec (predictable) with 99th percentile latency <250ms for our standard gen use-case.
- Isolation: network-level separation (VPC/NAT), customer KMS + audit logs retained 90 days.
- Autoscale / burst behavior: support bursts up to 2000 requests/sec for up to 2 hours without cold-start penalties.
- Cost predictability: committed pool pricing (monthly) with documented burst billing policy.

Proposed pilot scope (what Redwood can deliver in 4 weeks)
1) Reserved GPU pool sized to match baseline (we'll propose a CPU/GPU mix in the attached capacity spreadsheet).
2) Technical workshop to validate tokenization, KV cache strategy, and end-to-end latency. (Neha will run this).
3) Audit/KMS integration guide + sample IAM policy.
4) Pilot SOW and pricing draft for your procurement team.

Asks / outstanding items for you
- Can you share a 2-week sample of production traffic (timestamps + qps by endpoint)? (procured as tithonix-traffic-sample.csv suggested filename)
- Confirmation that 90-day audit log retention aligns with your compliance team.
- Procurement timeline & PO requirements (procurement contact).

Attachments: I attached a short Redwood Dedicated Quickstart and a pilot SOW template to give procurement and infra an early look.

Next steps (my recommended sequencing)
- You send the traffic sample and procurement contact (asha@ -> procurement cc ok).
- We schedule the technical workshop (2 hours) with your infra + tokenization lead — suggested window next week.
- I’ll send a draft SOW and a preliminary quote for committed pool sizing by EOD Monday.

If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll correct. Otherwise I’ll assume these bullets and move forward on the SOW/quote.

Thanks — appreciate the time.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-quickstart.pdf, pilot-sow-draft.docx
From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@tithonix.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procure@tithonix.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated pool discovery - Tithonix Labs

Thanks, Sergio — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Traffic sample: I'll export a 14-day sample this afternoon and put it on the shared Drive link. Expect both per-endpoint qps and an hourly aggregate.

2) Latency: the 99th jump we mentioned happens primarily on the /generate endpoint when batch jobs overlap with user traffic. We measure ~700–900ms currently. Our SLO ask is to get that below 300ms at 99th under baseline conditions — the 250ms you propose is ideal, but procurement/execs will accept <=300ms if the cost delta is reasonable.

3) Isolation / compliance: Confirmed — anything that processes PII must be isolated and tied to our KMS. 90-day retention is acceptable. We will need an SOC2 questionnaire answered as part of procurement (procurement cc’ing).

4) Burst: Bursts are irregular; typical baseline is ~750 rps, spikes to ~2200 for 1–3 hours at month end. We need burst headroom without manual intervention. Important: we cannot have long cold-starts during burst.

Procurement timeline: target decision by the end of December. We'll need a 30-day pilot agreement and internal PO process for pilots. Procurement contact is procurement@tithonix.com.

Please include Marissa on the quote/commercial thread — she'll lead pricing negotiations.

Thanks — Asha

--
Asha Reddy
Head of ML Platforms | Tithonix Labs
asha.reddy@tithonix.com
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@tithonix.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement <procure@tithonix.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated pool discovery - Tithonix Labs

Thanks Asha — great context and clear asks. Quick updates and concrete next steps: 

1) Traffic sample: once you drop the CSV to the Drive link above I’ll have Neha run a quick sizing model and produce two pool proposals: Baseline (committed) + Burst reserve (hot capacity with documented billing behavior). ETA: Monday 11/23 EOD.

2) SLOs: we'll target the 250ms 99th for the baseline proposal; we will also include a fallback SLT (<=300ms) for the cost-optimized option so you can see tradeoffs. Neha will validate the KV cache and tokenization plan at the workshop.

3) Compliance: attaching the SOC2 scoping checklist we typically provide; Neha will follow up with the audit logs/KMS integration notes in the tech workshop.

4) Pilot commercials & timeline: I’ll send a 30-day pilot SOW + quote (DocuSign) by Monday morning for procurement review. If that looks OK, we can stand up the reserved pool within 2 weeks of PO execution.

Proposed immediate scheduling:
- Technical workshop (2 hours) — Tue 11/24 10am PT or Wed 11/25 2pm PT. Please confirm which works.
- Commercial touchpoint (30 mins) — Wed 11/24 11:30am PT with Marissa and procurement to review SOW & billing.

Deliverables I’ll produce by Monday: capacity proposals (PDF), pilot SOW (DocuSign link), preliminary quote.

If this plan looks good I’ll proceed and copy the links off the HubSpot deal page for reference.

Appreciate the clear priorities — we’ll keep burst behavior and isolation as gating criteria.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
